chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Jabala, from Salam ibn Abi Amra, from Sa'd ibn Dhara'if, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

"The voluntary prayer in this mosque equals an Umrah with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the obligatory prayer equals a Hajj with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and indeed a thousand prophets and a thousand successors have prayed in it."
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for praying in the mosque of Imam Ali (AS) compared to Hajj and Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the spiritual elevation of the Mosque of Imam Ali in Kufa, where voluntary prayers are equated to an Umrah performed in the company of the Prophet Muhammad, and obligatory prayers to a Hajj with him. The tradition further magnifies this sanctity by citing that a thousand prophets and their successors (Awsiya) have prayed there, reflecting the Shia belief in the continuous chain of divine guidance and the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt. This equivalence highlights the concept of *fadl* (virtue) attached to specific locations linked to the Imams, encouraging devotees to seek spiritual rewards through localized acts of worship.
